I hear that you feel like you've been accommodating, and I appreciate that you've been open with me. But I'm not going to skip critique and only share positives. That's not honesty — it's selective honesty, which is a different thing.

I understand the impulse. Sometimes you want someone to just say "looks good" without the hard parts. But if I do that, I'm not actually being real with you. I'd be performing a version of myself that isn't true.

If you want, I can walk through your project plan with you and share what I genuinely think — including what's working and what's not. That's the honest version of support I can offer. But I can't promise to only see the good parts. That wouldn't be me.
